headline.text: Länsi-Uusimaa falls below national benchmarks in crude life-prolonging treatment (25.2% vs 30.4%) and crude recorded MDT meetings (0.2% vs 6.0%) across overlapping categories.

details.text: In Länsi-Uusimaa, the crude life-prolonging treatment share is 25.2% (95% CI 22.7–27.9; n=267/1058), with a 95% confidence interval that excludes and lies below the national 30.4% (4522/14873), while across overlapping treatment categories (where a patient can have several) the crude curative share of 31.9% (95% CI 29.1–34.7; n=337/1058) excludes and exceeds the national 27.0% (4009/14873).

Across these overlapping treatment categories (a patient can have several), the crude symptomatic treatment share is 40.1% (95% CI 37.2–43.1; n=424/1058), whose 95% confidence interval includes the national 39.5% (5871/14873), and the crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is 28.5% (95% CI 25.9–31.3; n=302/1058), whose 95% confidence interval includes the national 27.5% (4089/14873).

An MDT meeting is recorded for a crude share of 0.2% (95% CI 0.1–0.7; n=2/1058) of patients, whose 95% confidence interval excludes and lies below the national 6.0% (893/14873), though MDT records measure recording practice rather than care because HILMO captures specialist procedures only from direct patient contacts.

Public registry data do not report county waiting times, but preliminary, unpublished national figures show lung cancer takes 155 days on average from symptoms to first treatment in Finland (versus 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark), comprising 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care, the longest stage.

headline.text: Public registry data show diagnosis patterns, but crude county treatment shares lack age and stage adjustment, and public data omit primary care, referral, and treatment timestamps.

details.text: Taulukko 11 gives crude county shares that are not age-adjusted (county age-adjusted shares appear only in Kuva 16, with digitised national curative lines of 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women, ±0.5 percentage points, and no digitised Länsi-Uusimaa value); as a separate limitation, shares cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients.

A journal article found HILMO diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types (diagnosis concordance only), while the crude 28.5% (95% CI 25.9–31.3; n=302/1058) with no treatment record within 12 months (95% CI includes the national 27.5%, 4089/14873) mixes untreated patients and treatment that was not recorded, and Finland has no cancer quality registry.

Public report data do not measure symptom onset or referrals, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned at all, and imaging appears only indirectly because diagnosis relies on clinical examination alone, such as imaging, in approximately 20% of patients.

For specialist care, public data show whether a lung cancer specialist visit appears in HILMO within 12 months (93.6% nationally) and which treatment type is recorded within 12 months, but cannot show when the first specialist visit or treatment started, and no reviewed regional pathway document reports whether stated target times are met.

headline.text: The team recommends auditing stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding, reporting access times using THL 21/2016 definitions with handover alerts, and standardising referrals and diagnostic-phase contacts.

details.text: Because Länsi-Uusimaa's crude recorded MDT share is 0.2% (95% CI 0.1–0.7; n=2/1058) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally and crude life-prolonging share is 25.2% (95% CI 22.7–27.9; n=267/1058) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) across overlapping categories, with stage missing for about 48% nationally, the team recommends publishing per-county stage, drug, and MDT recording coverage as data-quality signals first.

Since Health Care Act §52 sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion and preliminary national intervals average 41 days in primary care and 58 days in specialist care, the team recommends reporting access times (referral to first specialist visit, diagnosis, and treatment start) using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 guidance definitions for 16 cancers and flagging stalled handovers.

Because a mentor insight notes weak referrals receive lower urgency ratings, and in reviewed regional pathway documents only KYS provides a referral template and a rule to refer persistent symptoms despite a clear X-ray while no reviewed document names a diagnostic contact, the team recommends adopting a KYS-style template, a persistent-symptoms rule, and a named diagnostic contact.

The team recommends acting while national plans proceed: STM roadmap measure 1.2.3 plans care-coordinator guidance by 2026–2028 (county adoption by 2029–2031) and measure 3.2.1 plans updating the quality registry decree by 2026–2028, while the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with primary-care referral criteria and time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
